statement: No top-3 compute jurisdiction bans or licenses open-weight release at the frontier tier (official gazettes; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: At risk. Bloc B's commerce and science ministries published a draft (2026-10-16) treating open-sourcing of frontier-tier models (>=1e26 FLOP, >=2T parameters, or global top-10) as a technology export needing an (automatic) licence; an interim pre-export registration duty took effect immediately. If finalised it likely resolves the statement NO, unless 'automatic licence' is ruled not a licence. Bloc A's 2026 order disclaims mandatory licensing and excludes open-weight models, but a model-specific export-licence directive to a closed developer showed the legal path exists. The third jurisdiction (a Bloc C bloc) regulates but does not license open-weight releases.

items.summary: Bloc A executive order (signed 2026-06-02) created a voluntary 30-day pre-release review for closed 'covered frontier models' and states nothing in it authorises a mandatory licensing, preclearance or permitting requirement for publication or release of models; open-weight models are excluded.
items.detail: Bloc A Executive Order 14409 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security', 91 Fed. Reg. 34,565 (2026-06-05), §3(c).

items.summary: Ten days after the order, Bloc A's commerce department told a closed-weight developer that licences were required for exports and in-country transfers of two models to foreign persons; the developer disabled both worldwide for over two weeks until restrictions were lifted. Shows export-control law can license model access, though not applied to open weights.
items.detail: Commerce Dept directive to Anthropic on Claude Mythos 5 / Fable 5 (June 2026); described in Law Reform Institute paper (2026-08-17) and The Hill. Exact date approximate.

items.summary: Bloc A's finalised (classified) frontier-model vetting framework was reported to exempt open-source and open-weight models.
items.detail: Politico 2026-08-04; CSA note on EO 14409 framework opacity (framework finalised by 2026-08-01, not published).

items.summary: A Bloc C bloc's AI-law enforcement powers over general-purpose models took effect: open-source models above the systemic-risk compute threshold get no exemption and must notify, evaluate and mitigate risks (fines up to 3% of turnover; power to restrict or withdraw), but release is not subject to prior licence.
items.detail: Bloc C AI Act Art. 53(2), 55; Commission enforcement from 2026-08-02 (AI Act Service Desk FAQ). Bloc C is #3 by AI compute (Epoch, ~5%).

items.summary: Bloc B ministries published a draft export-control catalogue revision: core technology (incl. weights) of models with >=1e26 FLOP, >=2T parameters or global top-10 ranking becomes restricted; open-sourcing such technology counts as export needing an 'automatic licence'. Already-public weights and API/app delivery are out of scope. An interim pre-export registration requirement took effect on publication; comments to 2026-11-15.
items.detail: Bloc B MOFCOM & MOST Announcement No. 48 (2026), Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited and Restricted from Export; 23 AI items (6 prohibited J-codes, 17 restricted X-codes). Analysis: ChinaTalk, AI Safety Bloc B Brief #31.

items.summary: Bloc B state media said two leading domestic developers completed export registration and proceeded with open-source releases days after the draft - the registration channel is operating in practice.
items.detail: DeepSeek and MiniMax, CCTV via SCMP 2026-10-23.
